name: Usercentrics
description: Usercentrics is a consent management platform for collecting, documenting, and applying website and application users' privacy choices.
agentUseSummary: Usercentrics is unavailable as a Relay agent connection because its published integration surface centers on browser and app SDKs that initialize a CMP and collect or change an end user's consent. Its server-side analytics export is a plan-gated raw-consent feed provisioned through support, not a bounded configuration-management API. Relay does not simulate consent, expose controller IDs or consent strings, or ingest raw consent histories.

blocked.label: Connect Usercentrics
blocked.description: Relay exposes no Usercentrics connection without a documented bounded server-side management API suitable for agent use.

blocked.label: Collect or change consent
blocked.description: Accept, deny, save, restore, reset, and every other end-user consent or session action are never executed by an agent.

blocked.label: Read private consent data
blocked.description: Controller IDs, device audit IDs, user sessions, consent histories, consent strings, service decisions, location, raw exports, and webhook payloads are excluded.

blocked.label: Use undocumented interfaces
blocked.description: Browser-observed configuration endpoints, internal GraphQL, arbitrary Usercentrics hosts, SDK network traffic, scraping, and reverse-engineered requests are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Usercentrics action or credential path is exposed until the provider publishes a stable bounded server-side management contract that does not require Relay to impersonate a consenting user or ingest raw consent histories.

runtimeSupport.description: No wrappers are mounted because the documented SDKs act in end-user consent sessions and the server-side export contains raw consent data.
No wrappers are mounted because the documented SDKs act in end-user consent sessions and the server-side export contains raw consent data.

providerSetup.blocker: Usercentrics documents client SDKs for initializing a CMP and accepting, denying, saving, restoring, or inspecting individual consent state. Its separate Analytics Data Export Service is a premium or corporate raw-consent export that requires support activation and specially delivered credentials; the public documentation does not establish a bounded server-side configuration-management API for Relay.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep Usercentrics unavailable and do not collect settings IDs, analytics IDs, API keys, controller IDs, sessions, consent strings, exports, or webhooks. Re-evaluate only if Usercentrics publishes a stable versioned server-side admin API with metadata-only reads, least-privilege credentials, fixed schemas, pagination and rate limits, revocation, and an explicit prohibition boundary around individual consent actions and histories.

evidence.supports: The official Browser SDK initializes from a settings ID and exposes accept-all, deny-all, and service-decision updates inside a browser consent session rather than a server-side admin contract.
The official Apps SDK is configured with a Settings ID or Ruleset ID and loads consent UI/configuration into an end-user device runtime.

Usercentrics says its scheduled API export contains raw analytics/consent data, is plan-gated, requires support activation, and delivers an Analytics ID and API key through a verified confidential process.
The official Consent Webhook is a plan-gated push of user consent payloads, not a bounded configuration metadata API.
